Subject: RFP: Subprocessor consolidation & regional edge provider assurances

Hi Thomas / GreenLeaf procurement team,

Thanks for the detailed RFP — attached are the items you requested to address the subprocessor and third‑party section. In summary: we are consolidating several edge routing and caching responsibilities to a single regional partner (EdgeCloudCo) for APAC to improve latency and cost predictability. The key points in the attached package (redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v2.xlsx + edge_region_transition_plan.pdf) are:

- Inventory: full vendor list (hosting, telemetry, metrics, CDN, edge inference partner) with contractual role designation and data access level.
- Risk controls: flow‑down requirements (encryption at rest/in transit, annual pen tests, vulnerability SLAs, incident notification windows).
- Migration plan: phased canary in APAC, fallbacks to multi‑region hosted endpoints, rollback criteria and SLO guardrails.

Specific notes for the RFP Q-section: Q12 (subprocessor listing) — see the inventory tab. Q14 (notification) — we commit to 30 days advanced notice for non‑critical changes and 7 days for critical security patches that may affect data residency. Q18 (attestations) — we can provide SOC 2 Type II for our platform and will request a copy of EdgeCloudCo's most recent attestation for your review.

Next steps: please let me know if you want a short technical deep dive with Karthik next week (30 min) to walk the architecture and the KV cache residency model. If acceptable, we can target a Nov 20 canary start for APAC edge routing.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attached inventory. A couple of clarifying questions before we book a call:

1) EdgeCloudCo — do you have a copy of their most recent SOC 2 / ISO attestation or an equivalent third‑party assurance? We need that for our vendor acceptance board.
2) Contractual flow‑down: will Redwood require EdgeCloudCo to accept the same data processing terms (DPA clauses) — specifically data deletion, audit rights, and breach notification timelines? We need explicit language to map to our legal review.
3) KV cache / ephemeral storage: the RFP asked if any customer PII could be written to edge caches. Can you confirm whether any decrypted customer content could be persisted on the edge nodes? If so, how is it protected and for how long?

We can do a 30‑minute technical review on Wed or Thu — Thomas preferred.

Regards,

Thomas — thanks for the questions. Technical clarifications below (will be happy to expand on the call):

1) Attestation: EdgeCloudCo maintains a SOC 2 Type II report for their control plane and physical data centers; we are coordinating to obtain the latest report and will deliver it under NDA. Redwood's platform also publishes our SOC 2 Type II boundary which covers the inference runtime and orchestration layer.

2) Flow‑downs: yes — Redwood requires contractual flow‑downs for processors that have logical access to customer content. Our standard DPA includes deletion/return obligations, audit/cooperation rights, and a 72‑hour incident notification window. We include a mandatory security appendix for any subprocessor handling decrypted payloads.

3) KV cache / PII: we do not persist customer PII to disk on edge nodes by default. The edge layer uses an in‑memory KV cache for model context (TTL configurable per customer). If a customer chooses to enable persistent caching for performance, that requires explicit configuration and additional contractual protections; we document that as an opt‑in in the attached scoping statement. All in‑memory caches are encrypted in transit and accessible only to the inference process; in‑memory contents are zeroed on process termination and not written to local persistent storage.

4) Fallback & continuity: the routing layer supports automatic failover to the nearest regional hosted pool (Redwood hosted) and to a cold standby cluster. Rollback is automated, and we maintain point‑in‑time metrics to validate model outputs post‑rollback.

I attached a short scoping statement that explains what workloads require persistent caches vs ephemeral caching (edgecloud_scoping_statement.docx). Happy to walk through on Wed 11/04 10:00 AM PT or Thu 11/05 9:00 AM PT.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
